Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (837 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that on November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards.
  • "Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.
  • Daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards. The occasion was the world premiere of "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" (released in the US and India as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone").

"Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.

Daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle. The BBC quoted him as saying, "It is so cool. I have never heard my name shouted so much in an hour.".

The crowds showed just how far Harry Potter fever had spread in only four years.

The first Harry Potter book was published by Britain's Bloomsbury in June 1997, with an initial print run of just 500 hardcover copies.

About 5,000 paperback copies were also released around the same time.

Today, first editions are prized collectors' items, with hardcover copies commanding high prices at auction. In mid-October, one sold for $400,000 through US auction house Heritage Auctions.

In a recent development, at first, the book's popularity grew largely by word of mouth among schoolchildren. Media attention followed when it won the prestigious Nestle Smarties Book Prize later that year.

With an estimated 120 million-plus copies sold worldwide, it is the best-selling book in the series and ranks among the best-selling novels of all time.

For years, J.K. Rowling's public image was defined by her extraordinary rise from a single mother on welfare to a billionaire.

Recent findings suggest that but in recent years, debate over her views on gender and transgender identity has increasingly overshadowed that success. It's an glitch Rowling herself frequently weighs in on.

In an essay published on her website on October 21, 2026, Rowling reiterated her opposition to what she calls the "current, dominant strain of trans activism." She argues that this movement "holds that a man who declares himself a woman is, literally, a woman, and is therefore entitled to be treated as a woman in all contexts." Rowling argues that allowing trans women into single-sex spaces poses a risk. She describes biological sex as an indisputable biological fact.

Such statements have led critics to accuse Rowling of transphobia, while others regard her stance as a defense of women's rights and safety.

According to recent reports, the controversy has also divided her fans. Some stand by Rowling, while others try to draw a distinction between the books and their author.

Others have left Harry Potter behind altogether. One former fan is German YouTuber Coldmirror, known for her Harry Potter parodies. The media artist from the Bremen area, whose real name is Kathrin Fricke, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper: "I don't have any love left for Harry. I'm still somewhat interested, but I can no longer watch it in good conscience." She cited Rowling's campaigning against transgender people as the reason.

Sources indicate that the "Harry Potter" film cast is divided as well. The three main stars — Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint — have publicly spoken out in support of transgender people. Meanwhile, Ralph Fiennes, who played Lord Voldemort, and Helena Bonham Carter, who portrayed Bellatrix Lestrange, have defended Rowling's right to express her views.

Despite the controversy surrounding Rowling, Warner Bros., which holds the Harry Potter film rights, is bringing the books back to the screen — this time as a series for HBO. The premiere is scheduled for December 25.

Sources indicate that the eight-episode first season is an an adaption of the first book. Even though the episode lengths haven't been announced, the scope of a TV series gives each book much more room than the original films did. That means more time to explore subplots, character development and everyday life at Hogwarts. While many fans are looking forward to a more detailed adaptation, others remain skeptical. They find it hard to imagine the familiar characters being played by anyone else.

The new trio consists of Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley.

J.K. Rowling is an executive producer on the show. HBO says, however, that her views on gender identity won't be reflected in the storyline. Several people involved in the new production have publicly distanced themselves from her views. Paapa Essiedu, who has been cast as Severus Snape, signed an open letter supporting transgender people. Rowling subsequently stated she had neither the power nor the desire to have him removed from the show because of it. John Lithgow, who plays Dumbledore, and Nick Frost, who portrays Hagrid, have also spoken out against Rowling's views.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, the Harry Potter merchandising machine is still going strong. On November 4, Britain's largest Harry Potter store to date is set to open in London. According to Warner Bros., the two-story shop covers more than 1,950 square meters.

This article was originally written in German.

Gian Piero Gasperini, speaking to DAZN after Parma-Roma (1-5), was pleased with his team’s victory.

Recent findings suggest that “A lot, because there’s always a bit of uncertainty when so many players leave and some return at the last minute. Then you have to figure out if you can pick up where you left off. Today’s result doesn’t reflect how difficult the match was because we faced a very determined Parma side, in excellent condition, who started very strongly. Then, over the 90 minutes, the game took a different turn, but there were moments of great balance.”.

The Grugliasco coach on the final step towards growth: “There are undoubtedly many details, some team-related, some individual, but there’s no doubt that this is a team that’s growing in every aspect. Even in difficult situations, we conceded a bad goal, and there could have been a psychological impact, but instead we reacted very strongly. That’s the best aspect: this team has the confidence to score goals, and even in the face of bad luck, they always have the conviction to move forward.”.

Recent findings suggest that gian Piero Gasperini on Malen: “But he was still an incredible player even before coming here, just look at his career path, first in Holland and then at Dortmund. You don’t go to certain teams. If you don’t have outstanding qualities, I probably put him where he performs best, not that he didn’t do well at other teams.”.

The Grugliasco-born coach concluded on Serie A forwards and the comparison with the Dutch center-forward: “In the Italian league, the numbers speak for themselves. There’s a great lineup of forwards in Serie A too. Lautaro comes to mind. He’s extraordinary right now and he combines with us. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cristiano Ronaldo is now just 14 goals away from reaching 1,000 goals, the landmark he has openly targeted as the defining achievement of the last years of his career. It now becomes his final challenge following his announcement that he’ll retire from the Portugal national team.

Industry observers note that at 41, the question is no longer whether Ronaldo can reach the four-figure mark. It is how long it will take him to get there.

The Portuguese superstar remains prolific for Al-Nassr, having taken his tally to 985 with a hat-trick in a 5-3 victory over Al Kholood on October 29th.

He recently confirmed that his 23-year international career is over, announcing his decision in an emotional farewell message to Portugal’s supporters.

“The time has come to hang up our national team’s number 7 shirt,” Ronaldo wrote, admitting that it had not been an easy decision.

That leaves Al-Nassr as his only remaining route to the 1,000-goal milestone, barring any change of heart over his international retirement or a farewell appearance for Portugal.

We’ve crunched the numbers and mapped out the various scenarios.

“I want to reach 1,000 goals,” Ronaldo said, unveiling his last major career ambition on Rio Ferdinand’s YouTube channel just over two years ago.

“If I don’t have any injuries, this for me is the most important [thing], I want that. For me, the best mark that I can have in football is to reach, first, 900 goals. After, my challenge is to be at 1,000 goals.

Industry observers note that “All the goals I have scored, they have video. They all have video. Listen, I respect all of them [Pele and Di Stefano]. And if you want more goals, I can bring them from training, too. And I will prove to the people after. They prefer this player, or this is the best one. I don’t care about that.”.

Ronaldo has maintained the importance of that ambition, previously identifying it alongside winning another Nations League title as a major motivation. The latter is now off the table, but his pursuit of four figures remains very much alive.

“Both aims are important,” he noted.

“One thousand goals, yes, and the national team. Winning the Nations League, the competition starts tomorrow [Thursday], it’s a fresh age.”.

With all that in mind, here’s our calculations for when Ronaldo could potentially reach the milestone of 1000 goals in his professional career.

Recent findings suggest that – Barring any major career-ending injuries, Ronaldo still looks likely to reach the milestone of a thousand goals at some point in 2027. Possibly as early as January or February, particularly if he maintains his recent scoring form.

Sources indicate that – It’s possible that if Ronaldo enjoys a resurgence and goes on a hot streak akin to his most prolific peak at Real Madrid, he could do it before the end of the year. His goal against Al Ahli took him to 986, leaving him with 14 to find, although his missed penalty in the same game was a reminder that even the most reliable goalscorers have off days. He would still need 14 goals in little over a month, though.

– If you take his recent rate of scoring (27 goals in 42 appearances during the calendar year of 2026) as what he’ll likely maintain, another 22 appearances would be required to score the remaining 14 goals. That would take us through to around February or March 2027. Crucially, that calculation previously allowed for further Portugal appearances, which can no longer be taken for granted.

Industry observers note that – There is an argument that Ronaldo could be set to improve upon that scoring rate. He’s been written off on the international stage after poor showings in the last two major summer tournaments, but he scored eight goals in nine games in the 2024-25 Nations League and a further five goals in qualifying for the 2026 World Cup. Although his international career is now over, rediscover that form in the Saudi Pro League, up his rate to around 1.00 goals per game and fill his boots for Al-Nassr, and Ronaldo could conceivably reach four figures early in 2027. At that rate, he’d need just 14 more appearances.

– There is a counter-argument that Ronaldo will instead slow down in these final furlongs of his career. His latest outing against Al Ahli offered evidence of both sides of that argument: he scored, but also missed a penalty in a 3-1 defeat. His 27 goals in 42 appearances in 2026 work out at 0.64 goals per game. Maintain that rate, and he’ll need another 22 games to score the 14 goals required to reach number one thousand. That should be comfortably achievable before the end of Al-Nassr’s 2026-27 campaign, which is due to end in late May 2027.

In a recent development, – The biggest unknown is now how prolific Ronaldo can remain at club level. His international retirement means he’ll no longer have the opportunity to add goals in Portugal colours, although it should also give him more time to concentrate on Al-Nassr and potentially manage his workload. Whether that makes him even more prolific in Saudi Arabia is another matter.

According to recent reports, – What kind of form he’ll show to get there is ultimately anyone’s guess. His goal against Al Ahli was his second in consecutive outings after the hat-trick against Al Kholood, but the missed penalty and defeat offered a less convincing reminder of his current form. The end of his international career removes one variable from our projections, while leaving the exact date far from certain.

– We’ll hedge our bets and estimate that Ronaldo’s form over the coming months will be somewhere between his spectacular peak and a severe decline. He is playing in the Saudi Pro League, after all, and his team is set up to feed him chances. With no more international fixtures to factor into the equation, we’re backing him to keep ticking along for Al-Nassr. With just 14 goals left to score, and having found the net again despite a frustrating evening against Al Ahli, we’re sticking with February 2027 as our tentative prediction for Ronaldo’s 1,000th career goal, although the loss of potential Portugal appearances could yet push that date back.

Breaking: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat said.
  • In a recent development, themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a big win.
  • "It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat said. "Making history once is something, but making it twice is really something else. I felt very happy and I felt a significant relief. Only I know how many sacrifices I made and how many hardships I needed to overcome.".

In a recent development, themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a big win. In Mariam Bsharat's case, it's about more than just dedication to training and taking care of the body. The 17-year-old won her second under-21 World Karate Championship gold medal competing for the Palestine national team in Poland in October.

"It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.

"I faced challenges in transportation," Bsharat stated. "I wasn't able to go from one city to another to be able to train with other people, so that I can actually prepare for competitions. I needed to travel to other countries like Jordan or Egypt ... which was very hard for me. And, financially, the support wasn't really the support an elite athlete needed.".

In a recent development, growing up in Nablus, Bsharat had a narrow path to the top. But initially, it was her own reluctance that threatened to stop a champion career before it started.

"When I was a little kid, I did not really love it," mentioned Bsharat, who competes in the division for fighters who weigh under 66 kilograms (145 pounds).

"I started it because my family was in that sport," Bsharat stated. "My father had a dojo, and my mother also did that sport. My siblings and my aunts and my uncles — it's a family thing. I started it because they were all doing it. In time, I started getting into it.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that family has been a constant source of comfort and inspiration for Bsharat. Her father and uncle have acted as manager and coach respectively. While her mother and siblings moved with Mariam to Hamburg, Germany, last year, her father remained in order to take care of his business, the dojo, though he visits and tries to be with his daughter in competitions. Integration has been made easier by her mastery of the language, taught to her by her German mother.

Bsharat has mixed feelings about leaving her homeland.

Sources indicate that "I'm thankful to be here because being in Germany opened lot of doors for me, and I think I have a brighter future here," Bsharat stated. "But also being in Palestine was just my everyday life, and I loved it there. My family was around me, my friends were around me, and I just felt comfortable, which was a significant change coming here to Germany. I think every change comes with hardships.".

As well as the obvious difficulties of living in an area occupied by Israel, there are particular challenges for sportspeople living in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with access to facilities, travel and constant security fears among them. As such, very few people from the Palestinian territories become successful on the international sporting stage. That, Bsharat noted, gives her responsibilities that are unusual and heavy for a person of any age, let alone a 17-year-old.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"Being an elite athlete in Palestine is something very special because not everybody in Palestine has that opportunity. There aren't really a lot of athletes that are elite and who win international medals,” Bsharat noted.

It has been revealed that "So all that pressure from all the country and all the people, the family, the coaches are on me because I'm representing them, raising their flag,” she stated. "I sometimes even forget to fight for myself and actually think about myself.".

Industry observers note that that has not yet proved a barrier to Bsharat, who is is ranked first in the world in her category by the World Karate Federation (WKF). With Palestine recognized by the International Olympic Committee, Bsharat would likely have been a contender to raise that flag in Los Angeles at the 2028 Olympics. But the sport was dropped from the Games in 2024.

According to recent reports, "The global karate community remains steadfast in our belief that the natural place for karate is within the Olympic Games, and we sincerely hope that the incongruence we suffered in Paris 2024 and LA 2028 will be corrected for Brisbane 2032, if not sooner," the WKF wrote in response to the decision in 2024. The sport was also taken off the slate for the recent Youth Games in Senegal.

Should karate return in Brisbane, Bsharat would likely be approaching her prime. In the meantime, she is looking forward to starting her journey as a senior when she turns 18. But she won't be hanging around.

"My goal is it to be a world champion at seniors, which is the hardest and the best thing you can achieve in karate," she remarked.

"But winning an Olympic medal, being called Olympic champion or just representing my country with that flag [is a thought that] is just full of happiness and pride.".

The interview was conducted by Janek Speight.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It looks increasingly as though the Premier League could be a cakewalk for the reigning champions Arsenal – whether or not Manchester City are handed a points deduction.

Man City went into the last international break with a 100% winning record under newly introduced manager Enzo Maresca, with it all looking like business as usual following the departure of their era-defining manager Pep Guardiola at the end of last season.

However, things have taken a severe dip after the news broke that the club have been found guilty of the vast majority of their 115 charges.

The Athletic’s David Ornstein originally broke the news over October’s extended international break, and a few days later the Premier League confirmed it with a statement that could have massive repercussions for the English top flight.

“An independent Commission has found Manchester City FC guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League’s investigation,” read their statement.

Any potential sanctions are yet to be confirmed or confirmed, while Man City have lodged an appeal against the verdict, having stated that they’re “both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission” and continuing to protest their innocence.

According to recent reports, city responded in a defiant mood, having extended their winning run by going to Anfield and beating Liverpool 3-0. But a few days later, they were defeated 4-2 to PSG in the Champions League and a serious domestic slump has followed.

Maresca’s men have now suffered three successive Premier League defeats, a run that started with a 2-1 defeat away to Aston Villa. Losses to Brighton and Nottingham Forest followed, before a 1-1 draw at home to Fulham brought that losing streak to an end.

The result leaves them five points behind Arsenal at this fledgling stage of the Premier League campaign. The Gunners have won nine of their 10 league outings, are consistently keeping clean sheets, and the recent form is ominous.

The question of a points deduction when it comes to a Premier League title race could soon be academic.

In a recent development, city have picked up just seven points from six matches since the verdict was announced in September. That’s eight fewer points than Mikel Arteta’s Gunners, three fewer than Tottenham, and fewer than the likes of Brighton, Bournemouth and Fulham. They are level with Everton.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in February 2011, Newcastle United completed one of the most incredible comebacks in Premier League history to draw 4-4 with Arsenal at St James’ Park. We want to know how well you remember the game.

Newcastle, who had just sold Andy Carroll to Liverpool, got off to a dreadful start and Arsenal’s Theo Walcott scored after 44 seconds.

Johan Djourou doubled their lead a couple of minutes later before Robin van Persie netted a brace to make it 4-0 inside the opening 26 minutes.

But Arsenal’s Abou Diaby received a red card at the start of the second half and the game completely changed. Alan Pardew’s side scored two penalties in the second half and their No.20 also found the back of the net from close range.

A midfielder then scored a stunning volley in the 87th minute to complete the comeback and rescue a point for Newcastle.

Industry observers note that “It was not how to approach a Premier League game,”  Newcastle manager Alan Pardew remarked after the game. “You have to pressure people, tackle people, turn people around [and] force them into errors. You can force any team into errors.

“Part of my [half-time] message was that you cannot sulk in front of 52,000 people at St James’ Park. They were letting themselves down more than anyone else. They showed to their family and friends that they are better than that.”.

Sources indicate that we’re now asking you to name Pardew’s XI from that draw with Arsenal. The time to beat from the Planet Football office is 02:11.

Celtic 4 St Mirren 1: Oxlade-Chamberlain rolls back the years as champions put Buddies to the sword

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026.

What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.

Celtic wins with bells and whistles attached have been as rare as hen’s teeth since this campaign began.

That the supporters witnessed one in trying circumstances felt significant given the arduous schedule which awaits in the coming six weeks.

It has been revealed that despite having no option but to piece together a midfield, O’Neill watched his side create a slew of opportunities. They took four with as many different scorers and might well have had more.

Sources indicate that A display brimming with enterprise and imagination boded well for what lies ahead. For the first time since September, Celtic have chalked up three straight wins. Ahead of the trip to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday, it appears that a bit of wind is back in the sails.

According to recent reports, this was as comprehensive a win as the scoreline suggests. The champions were never in danger from the moment Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain edged them in front just after the half hour mark.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain celebrates Celtic's first goal against St Mirren.

In danger of becoming something of a forgotten man, the former England man rolled back the years here with a display which reminded you why he once wore the shirts of Liverpool and Arsenal. On this evidence, he still has a contribution to make at Parkhead.

It has been revealed that the outcome was more or less settled by the interval. Camilo Duran continued his outstanding first season in Glasgow’s East End with another assured finish.

Luke McCowan, a man who’s not exactly had his critics to seek in recent times, netted the third before the break, his goal a just reward for a tidy afternoon’s work.

On a day when O’Neill would have had concerns about his midfield, Callum McGregor also netted with a crisp strike from the edge of the box.

St Mirren’s consolation, coming from Killian Phillips’ penalty, was too little too late.

On Friday, Buddies boss Craig McLeish had made some salient points about the self-interest which is holding back Scottish football.

It’s hard not to like McLeish’s attitude and the style of football his side are playing. But they are continuing to lose goals far too easily. They could find themselves getting dragged into trouble if they don’t quickly address it.

Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring their second goal in the 4-1 win.

In a recent development, on Friday, O’Neill had rejected the suggestion that Haissem Hassan had been omitted from the squad which faced Kilmarnock because he needed a kick up the backside. Yet, curiously, there was no sign of the Egyptian again here.

With Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur injured, O’Neill hoped that a combination of McGregor, McCowan and Oxlade-Chamberlain would have enough.

Kasper Hogh’s chances of ending a run of 16 games without a goal weren’t helped by him starting on the bench. He didn’t leave it.

With just one win in nine coming into this, Craig McLeish’s side were short on points yet they were not short on confidence.

Although they played some stuff which was very easy on the eye, an inability to keep the ball out of the net cost them dear again.

McCowan had an early shot blocked before Colby Donovan had a weak effort saved. McCowan also hesitated to take a first-time strike with Louis Jackson doing enough to protect Jacob Chapman’s goal.

It has been revealed that celtic actually had the ball in the net twice before they made it count. Duran planted a header and a shot in the visitors’ net only to discover that the offside flag had been raised.

Jota sparked a sweeping move which saw Yang Hyun-jun tee up McCowan. Paul Nsio became the latest Saints player to frustrate the Celtic midfielder with a block.

Sources indicate that saints were aggrieved that Yang won a free-kick by going to ground too easily just before the opener. They may have had a point. That didn’t excuse the defending which followed.

Cameron Carter-Vickers rolled the ball in Yang’s direction. The winger burst away from Declan John and assessed his options.

His cut-back for the unmarked Oxlade-Chamberlain was inch-perfect. The former England midfielder swept home his first goal since netting against the same opponent in April.

Saints might well have levelled immediately. Ismeal Kabia wriggled away from Donovan and picked out Eseosa Sule. Liam Scales did well to prevent the forward netting from seven yards.

Celtic then cut through Saints with embarrassing ease. A straight pass sent Yang clear on goal. He should have gone for glory, but instead tried to square the ball to allow Duran a tap-in. Alex Gogic had other ideas and knocked the ball away for a corner.

Celtic midfielder Luke McCowan and St Mirren's Paul Nsio battle for the ball.

McLeish’s hopes of making it to the break still in the contest unravelled in the final five minutes of the first period.

Kieran Tierney’s decision to swap flanks paid dividends with a brilliant in-swinging cross. Duran ghosted onto it and cushioned the ball beyond Chapman with his left foot to claim his 14th goal of his debut season.

Jota might well have made it three-nil seconds later and he fired Oxlade-Chamberlain’s lay-off straight at the keeper.

There was no hope for Chapman as Celtic all but wrapped up the win three minutes before the interval.

Industry observers note that tierney was again the provider, his energy taking him to the line and allowing him to cross. McCowan calmly stroked home his second goal of the season.

It has been revealed that saints kept going seeking a goal which might have made it interesting. Kabia’s strike forced Sam Johnstone into a smart stop down to his right.

Yang ought to have killed the contest but blazed over while leaning back. Skipper McGregor revealed him how to do it as he buried a right foot shot low in the bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the box after a defender had taken the ball off Duran’s toe.

Saints did get on the board thanks to Phillips’ penalty conversion, the award coming after Johnstone clattered Calvin Ramsay as he punched clear.

O’Neill was still able to send on Shim Mheaka and James Forrest with Austin Trusty returning to warm applause. Joel van den Berg had already been introduced for his debut along with Callum Osmand. The Dutch teenager highlighted up well.

The shocking Premier League table since Chelsea’s disastrous BlueCo takeover in 2022

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (772 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s been an interesting and uncertain few years at Chelsea since the BlueCo consortium completed a takeover of the club, ending Roman Abramovich’s ownership after almost two decades.
  • It has been revealed that the Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital-led ownership group inherited one of English football’s most successful clubs.
  • Recent findings suggest that boehly has since announced his decision to sell his shares and step away from the club, bringing another change to an ownership structure that has rarely been short of headlines.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been an interesting and uncertain few years at Chelsea since the BlueCo consortium completed a takeover of the club, ending Roman Abramovich’s ownership after almost two decades.

It has been revealed that the Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital-led ownership group inherited one of English football’s most successful clubs. What followed has been a period of extraordinary spending, managerial upheaval and wildly inconsistent results.

Recent findings suggest that boehly has since announced his decision to sell his shares and step away from the club, bringing another change to an ownership structure that has rarely been short of headlines. But the bigger question is what BlueCo have actually achieved since taking charge in 2022.

Industry observers note that abramovich was never afraid to sack a manager. There were frequent changes in the dugout during the Russian oligarch’s reign, but silverware was lifted frequently.

There were some lows, including a 10th place finish and trophyless campaign following Jose Mourinho’s meltdown in 2015-16, but generally the club were pretty consistently in the Champions League.

The club only failed to qualify for UEFA’s flagship competition twice during the Abramovich era, and they famously won it twice.

“We are honoured to become the new custodians of Chelsea Football Club,” new chairman Todd Boehly stated at the time.

“We’re all in – 100% – every minute of every match. Our vision as owners is clear: we want to make the fans proud.

In a recent development, “Along with our commitment to developing the youth squad and acquiring the best talent, our strategy of action is to invest in the club for the long term and build on Chelsea’s remarkable history of success. I personally want to thank ministers and officials in the British government, and the Premier League, for all their work in making this happen.”.

The latest ownership wasted little time making its mark. Thomas Tuchel was sacked, the squad that had lifted the Champions League trophy in 2021 was gradually dismantled, and hundreds of millions were spent on a wholesale rebuild.

Results weren’t immediately forthcoming. Graham Potter struggled to make an impact and Frank Lampard’s return proved a disaster. Chelsea finished 12th in the first year of the BlueCo era – lower than they ever finished in Abramovich’s reign.

There was progress the following year, following further investment and big-money signings like Moises Caicedo and Enzo Fernandez settling in, but Mauricio Pochettino couldn’t quite get them back into the Champions League and departed after just one season.

Year three of BlueCo’s ownership brought further improvements. Enzo Maresca led the Blues to a top-four finish as well as the UEFA Conference League and FIFA Club World Cup trophies, the latter delivered with a statement 3-0 victory over European champions PSG in the final.

However, it doesn’t appear that progress has been linear. Maresca departed in January, Chelsea limply exited the Champions League at the Round of 16, and his successor Liam Rosenior struggled badly for results.

A dire run cost the young coach his job after only a few months at the helm, while the financial implications of failing to qualify for Europe brought into sharp focus the viability of this entire project.

While individual seasons have offered reasons for optimism, the bigger picture makes for less comfortable reading.

Looking at the Premier League table since BlueCo took over, Chelsea have collected 244 points from 163 matches. That’s only eighth in the division, behind Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool, Aston Villa, Newcastle, Manchester United and Brighton.

Recent findings suggest that they have won just 68 of those 163 games, with 55 defeats. Brighton, a club who have received a reported £265million from Chelsea for players, managers and staff, have actually collected two more points over the same period.

Chelsea are also 115 points behind Arsenal. The gap has become a chasm.

Industry observers note that there have been some truly miserable afternoons along the way, too. Chelsea’s historic home defeats to Tottenham and Leeds this season are particularly difficult to reconcile with the club’s former standards. Losing to either rival at Stamford Bridge would once have been a major embarrassment. Losing to both underlines just how much has changed, and the pressure already mounting on Xabi Alonso.

Here’s the full table since BlueCo completed a takeover of the club.

#83160. What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

📅 04 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1070 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1070 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one glitch ranked above all others: the economy.
  • So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?
  • Recent findings suggest that markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one glitch ranked above all others: the economy.

So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?

Recent findings suggest that markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively. Global stocks rallied as investors appeared to take heart from the Democrats' victory.

With Democrats now holding comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress and Trump still in the White House, it could lead to gridlock in Washington. Trump has already noted he would become "Mr Veto," meaning he would block any legislation the Democrats advance.

"The magnitude of the gains for the Democrats in the midterms does not change too much for the near-term policy outlook, given the party still lacks a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate and President Trump has veto power to block legislation," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, said in a note.

"I think we are looking at two years of complete 100% gridlock," Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, nonresident senior fellow with the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told DW after the results came in. "Nothing will get done of any kind.".

It has been revealed that some investors appear worried that the Democrats could force through AI regulation, especially if they also win the White House in 2028. Rising opposition among large majorities of the US population to data centers — the key infrastructure behind AI — helped secure victories for many Democratic candidates.

Kirkegaard, who is also a senior fellow at Bruegel, a European economics think tank, remarked the vote showed the extent of that opposition. Even if the Democrats can't force regulation, he thinks local opposition will make it harder for data centers to be built, which could hit the valuation of major tech firms that have benefitted from the AI boom.

According to recent reports, "This election reveals that the political underpinning of the rapid, aggressive AI growth story is shaky," he remarked. "It doesn't mean it's going to stop or be made illegal, but the dynamic of the growth story has shifted.".

If the Democrats were to win the presidency in 2028, Brown said, they would be perfectly placed to make major policy changes. "That includes the potential for tax hikes on corporations and high-income individuals as well as regulation that could delay the AI rollout," he said.

According to polling conducted in early October by the Pew Research Center, 56% of Americans say Trump's tariff policies will have mostly negative impacts on the country, with only 20% saying mostly positive.

That sentiment clearly drove many Democrats to victory in the midterms — particularly in states where tariffs have had a particularly negative impact. That includes those with sectors reliant on exports, such as Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Illinois, where counter-tariffs have hit and those that have high trade volumes with Canada.

Yet, barring an unprecedented climbdown from Trump — who has been ideologically wedded to tariffs since he first became a public figure almost 50 years ago — it's not clear how the Democrats could force substantial change to the president's signature economic policy.

"Trump will not be moderated," Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore, told DW earlier this year. "Expect him to continue his trade disruption and tariff policies for as long as he remains in the Oval Office.".

Though the US Constitution gives Congress the power to collect and organize tariffs, various laws passed over the years have given presidents power to implement tariffs when they cite certain conditions, such as national security or economic emergencies.

In a recent development, trump has already used such avenues for his tariffs and can continue to do so, despite some legal rebukes. However, while Congress can't necessarily force an end to Trump's existing tariffs, it can now take further legal action against them to prevent greater escalation.

Though Trump and the Democrats are clearly not going to make common cause, Kirkegaard said, the scale of the Republicans' defeat might force Trump to be less erratic in his policymaking, from escalating his trade war with Canada to his Iran policy.

Trump stated in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeats that he would "work with" the Democrats and told the Financial Times in the run-up to the vote that he was unlikely to escalate the war in Iran.

Were a deal to be struck with Iran, soaring energy prices — a pivotal election problem — could finally fall, helping voters with their cost-of-living concerns.

According to recent reports, "You've got to get a deal with Iran, and you've got to bring down gas prices," Kirkegaard mentioned. "From a political point of view, that's the most important thing now.".

In a recent development, george Saravelos, an analyst with Deutsche Bank FX Research, thinks the markets are beginning to become more optimistic in that area. "With oil flows through the Middle East having materially recovered, the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium of re-escalation and energy supply disruption," he mentioned in a note.

Despite the scale of the Democrats' victory, the fact that Trump remains in the Oval Office will complicate all efforts to force a change to signature economic policies and concerns.

Sources indicate that yet Congress can now exert considerable pressure. Another matter vital to voters was corruption and the belief that the Trump administration has engaged in corruption and personal enrichment while in office.

That raises the prospect of the new Democratic-controlled Congress launching legal investigations and potentially pursuing another impeachment of Trump, which could force the president to negotiate on some economic issues to secure his political survival.

It has been revealed that "Can you find 10 or 12 Republican senators who, in the face of overwhelming corruption, would be willing to vote for articles of impeachment? I wouldn't rule it out," Kirkegaard mentioned. "And that's a scenario in which Trump might suddenly be much more accommodating to, for instance, abandoning most of his tariffs.".

Despite voters' clear rejection of Trump's economic policies, the Democratic Party's newly minted senators, congressmen and congresswomen face an uphill battle in trying to reverse them.

Bayern Munich’s treatment of Jamal Musiala is grim, depressing and utterly classless

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (841 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there are few things more exciting than watching an academy graduate develop into a superstar.
  • Sources indicate that he joined the club as a 16-year-old, grew into a world-class talent, has made over 200 first-team appearances and won six Bundesliga titles.
  • To a situation where Bayern’s hierarchy seem intent on unsettling one of their most valuable players and making his position at the club increasingly uncomfortable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there are few things more exciting than watching an academy graduate develop into a superstar. Bayern Munich got to experience exactly that with Jamal Musiala.

Sources indicate that he joined the club as a 16-year-old, grew into a world-class talent, has made over 200 first-team appearances and won six Bundesliga titles. For a time, he was the envy of Europe. It was only a couple of years ago that he was widely regarded as one of the finest young talents in the world.

So how did we get here? To a situation where Bayern’s hierarchy seem intent on unsettling one of their most valuable players and making his position at the club increasingly uncomfortable.

“We’re in a dilemma with him,” honorary president Uli Hoeness told BILD a couple of weeks ago.

“He has an illness that cannot simply be cured, but can be managed to some extent with medication. However, whether he will ever regain the level of performance he once had remains uncertain.”.

To understand the situation, you have to appreciate just how much Musiala has been through. His momentum was first halted by a devastating ACL injury at the 2025 Club World Cup, which saw him sidelined for half a season. He hasn’t quite ever recaptured his best form since returning to action.

Sources indicate that there have been further complications, too. Musiala revealed in August that he was being treated for a neurological dysfunction which causes temporary seizures, following two collapses during Bayern’s pre-season friendlies.

“The experience with such an injury suggests that it will be difficult for him to reach the level he had before,” Bayern legend Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has since stoked the fire.

“His high salary is no longer sustainable. Nobody will buy him under these conditions. The discussion hasn’t taken place yet, but we have to think about the finances.”.

Industry observers note that it is difficult to escape the feeling that Bayern’s hierarchy are turning the screw. German outlet BILD have subsequently reported that Musiala’s medication continues to cause problems, with recurring side effects proving problematic. Whether coincidental or otherwise, the steady drip-feed of negative headlines is doing little for the player.

Bayern have already made Harry Kane Europe’s highest-paid player and are reportedly keen to reward Michael Olise with a bumper new deal. The prospect of having Musiala on similarly astronomical wages is said to be a headache for the Bayern hierarchy.

Industry observers note that that is hardly Musiala’s problem. Contracts work both ways, and Bayern cannot expect players to honour their commitments only when it suits the club financially. They were happy to offer him those wages in the first place.

FIFPRO is the global representative organisation for professional footballers’ unions, advocating for players’ rights, welfare and working conditions around the world. They have struck the perfect tone.

“FIFPRO is deeply concerned by the repeated public statements from FC Bayern Munich’s leadership calling into question the contract of Jamal Musiala as he returns from injury,” they posted in a statement.

According to recent reports, “Bayern’s honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala’s contract in quick succession. In FIFPRO’s view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern’s standing should know better.

According to recent reports, “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player’s future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. Making Musiala’s health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

It has been revealed that “Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise. Clubs, leagues and player unions have agreed at FIFA level that contractual stability is a core principle of the game. It protects clubs as much as it protects players.

“FIFPRO stands with Jamal Musiala and with all players who honour their commitments. We expect their employers to do the same.”.

According to recent reports, they’ve absolutely nailed it. We couldn’t have put it better ourselves.

It has been revealed that bayern’s old guard are entitled to their opinions, but we’re equally entitled to call out behaviour that is utterly classless. Musiala is going through a horrible experience, battling a difficult medical condition while trying to get his career back on track – all the while feeling like his club doesn’t have his back.

According to recent reports, borussia Dortmund are top of the Bundesliga. Long may that continue as Bayern continue this sorry spectacle.

There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.

Sources indicate that this young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, Liverpool came from two goals behind, and it all ended with a panic that meant they came close to chucking it away again. But what everyone could agree on from this strange match of fluctuating fortunes was that Ngumoha looks like one of the best young players in Europe. He is also a bona fide two-sided winger, winning this game for Liverpool from the right wing rather than his conventional left-wing role.

Ngumoha created the second Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo and then the third for Mac Allister with the game’s best moment. That was an electrifying run into a group of converging yellow shirts in which he beat two men and still retained the composure to pick out Mac Allister in the area. Even as the Argentine ran to the Kop to celebrate, that stand was chanting the name of the teenager from east London. Ngumoha was one of three academy boys in Andoni Iraola’s XI, along with Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni, and all had an impact.

According to recent reports, iraola noted later that Ngumoha had taken care of the defensive work too against Sergi Cardona, an attacking left-back who scored his team’s second goal. From an attacking point of view, Iraola agreed, Ngumoha had periods of the game when he looked unstoppable. “If we can put Rio in situations one-v-one, he makes plays, [and] he produces things,” Iraola remarked. “The assist for Alexis is a lovely play. He could go down for a penalty but he decides to continue which is a great decision. Also endurance-wise he is able to play more minutes.”.

He becomes the youngest Liverpool player in Champions League history to register an assist in the competition. For Iraola it will be hard to leave Ngumoha out of the game against in-form Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday. “I believe in myself to do it,” Ngumoha mentioned to Amazon Prime TV. “The more chances we get, the more it makes the opposition worry. I just keep going and be ruthless.”.

Iraola would later bring on the three £100m attackers whom he had left on the bench, with Sunday’s game in mind. Florian Wirtz, a half-time arrival, scored the fourth and Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak would later come on. Hard to call how it might go at home to Brighton. Liverpool’s defending was erratic at times, but their comeback was impressive.

Iraola made major changes at half-time, substituting Araújo and playing without a conventional right-back for the second half. It was brave and changed the momentum of the game, pushing his team higher up the pitch in what looked like a man-to-man marking arrangement. It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. However much that was destabilising for Liverpool, by half-time they were level.

“They are so good on the ball,” Iraola noted of Villarreal afterwards. Indeed, Villarreal’s manager Iñigo Pérez, a former Athletic team-mate of the Liverpool manager, was a coach whom Iraola sought to appoint at Bournemouth. “People probably don’t rate them [Villarreal],” Iraola said, “but after Barça they are probably the best in La Liga. They have 61 per cent of possession. Probably they have not had the results they deserve. If you are not really aggressive, you are not going to get the ball.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t take as much risk. We were struggling because it is not a team that you can just press a bit. Either you go all the way or you will struggle without the ball.” Once Liverpool had done so, he said, his team had “won a lot of duels”. He was right in that respect. With the space squeezed, it was the power of Liverpool’s midfield that was telling.

In a recent development, virgil van Dijk gave the first goal to Villarreal’s small No 9 Georges Mikautadze who had looked up to that point like he was hopelessly mismatched against the Liverpool captain and Jérémy Jacquet. Van Dijk’s misjudged header back to Alisson let in the striker, who did well to gather the ball and then hit it early. The second Villarreal goal at the midpoint of the first half was a mistake from Kostas Tsimikas, who failed to step up and played both Mikautadze and Cardona onside from Nathan Saliba’s ball. Either might have tucked it in but it was the left-back Cardona who took it on.

Then came Ngumoha’s massive second half, creating the third for Mac Allister. The teenager went past Cardona and the substitute Juan Foyth in a couple of strides. Wirtz dispatched the fourth from Gakpo’s ball.

Even so there was still time for Liverpool to show that they had sacrificed some defensive stability. The absence of a right-back cost them when substitute Tani Oluwaseyi ran into that area of the pitch to score Villarreal’s third late on. The third win of Liverpool’s Champions League season puts them second in the 36-team super-table, and behind defending champions Paris St-Germain only on goal difference.

Liverpool are also seeing a fresh star emerge. Ngumoha might be the most expensive academy signing in the game’s modern history but alongside the £100m men he looks like a risk that was worth taking.

A very interesting team selection from Andoni Iraola. Liverpool’s head coach had indicated at his pre-match press conference that he was going to go as strong as possible, as his side seek to secure their third straight Champions League win. But the very fact Iraola has chosen to put Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola on the bench indicates he has one eye on Sunday’s demanding assignment against Brighton at Anfield.

It has been revealed that iraola will be delighted to have Cody Gakpo fit again and Lewis Koumas certainly deserves another opportunity to lead the line. But after victory’s against Atletico Madrid and LASK, Liverpool have given themselves some breathing space and it is understandable if Iraola, who has bemoaned the lack of time he has to train his squad, is already plotting Brighton’s downfall.

Industry observers note that the club known as the “Yellow Submarine” made themselves some fans in the red half of Merseyside by denying Everton a place in the Champions League proper in 2005/06. Everton lost 4-2 on aggregate, and there was controversy in the second leg in Spain when Pierluigi Collina disallowed a Duncan Ferguson header that could have taken the tie to extra time. Everton had finished fourth, one place above Liverpool, the previous season, but Liverpool’s triumph in Istanbul assured them of a qualification place too. Unlike Everton, they prevailed.

Speaking of which, Rafael Benitez is at Anfield this evening.

Dominic King takes stock of Andoni Iraola’s first 10 games in charge of Liverpool and, despite some teething problems, he believes there are reasons to be optimistic. The demands Iraola is putting on Liverpool’s midfielders are an interesting tactical wrinkle, with Dom writing: “Liverpool’s formation will always be written as 4-2-3-1, but the reality is that Iraola’s team do not play in four clear tactical lines. He asks specific jobs of his midfielders, deploying them detailed instructions, and it is going to require some patience before performances become consistent.”.

A precious victory at Brentford, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak among the goals and a couple of improved showings from Florian Wirtz mean things now look a little brighter for Liverpool.

They are strong favourites to make it nine points from nine in the Champions League by beating Villarreal at Anfield this evening, the Spanish club they vanquished in the 2022 semi-finals under Jürgen Klopp.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool drew Atletico Madrid at home (already ticked off) and Inter Milan away as their two pot-one fixtures, which is about as kind as you can expect. A top-two finish in the league phase is a realistic aspiration for Andoni Iraola’s team, and something would need to go badly awry for them to miss out on the top eight.

Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Isak returned from injury to strengthen Liverpool at Brentford, although Szoboszlai has been lost for a few weeks following another hamstring complication.

Villarreal have punched well above their weight in Europe for the past few decades, reaching two European Cup semi-finals (beaten by Arsenal in 2006 as well as Liverpool in 2022) and winning the Europa League under Unai Emery in 2021.

They have been mediocre in La Liga so far this season though, 12th after nine games on nine points and with a goal difference of zero. Their Champions League performances have been promising though, losing by the odd goal in a frantic finish at Borussia Dortmund and beating Napoli 3-1 at home. Villarreal’s best player is probably Senegalese central midfielder Pape Gueye, and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pépé is also in their ranks. Gueye, despite his position, is their joint-top scorer in all competitions with three goals.

Iraola will be up against his close friend and former Athletic Bilbao team-mate Inigo Perez who is now in charge at Villarreal. Perez was also Iraola’s assistant at Rayo Vallecano, the job which earned the Basque his move to Bournemouth. Perez guided Rayo Vallecano to the Uefa Conference League final last season.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It’s been quite the ride for Leeds since their return to the Premier League, but they comfortably stayed up last season and are now looking increasingly established at this level.
  • In the opening months of the 2025-26 campaign, Farke struggled to balance attack and defence as his side only took 11 points from their first 12 matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since Leeds United switched to a 3-5-2 formation, only a handful of Premier League clubs have accumulated more points than Daniel Farke’s side.

It’s been quite the ride for Leeds since their return to the Premier League, but they comfortably stayed up last season and are now looking increasingly established at this level.

In the opening months of the 2025-26 campaign, Farke struggled to balance attack and defence as his side only took 11 points from their first 12 matches.

During those first 12 games, Leeds often lined up in a 4-3-3 formation, which often left them looking vulnerable in defence.

With Leeds sat in the bottom three and Farke under increasing pressure, he made the switch to 3-5-2 during their trip to Manchester City in November.

While Leeds lost that game in the last minute thanks to a Phil Foden winner, Farke’s side indicated a competitive edge that they had been lacking in several of their previous games.

Since then, the German boss has stuck with the 3-5-2 formation and Leeds’ league form has taken a huge leap forward as a result.

According to recent reports, they went on a seven-game unbeaten streak in the Premier League immediately afterwards, which was their longest undefeated top-flight streak since 2001. They’ve since beaten that with an even longer unbeaten run.

Leeds went on to comfortably secure their Premier League status last season, and they’ve continued to build on that progress in 2026-27.

It has been revealed that farke’s side have established themselves in mid-table, presently sitting eighth with 50 points from 36 matches. They’ve lost just twice this season, although a tendency to draw games has prevented them from making a sustained push towards the European places.

In the Championship, Farke often stuck to his 4-2-3-1 formation, but conceded that he needed to be more adaptable in the Premier League.

“When we were winning most games [last season], we did not change our base formation much,” Farke told Sky Sports last season.

“The top teams in Europe and the Premier League always play the same formation.

“But you have to bridge this gap of individual quality, you have to be more flexible. This was clear at the beginning of the season. For that, we have trained a lot in a three-man formation. I knew we are prepared to switch between it in each and every game.”.

Farke’s side have now produced a stunning 4-1 away victory over Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, securing their first win at the ground in decades and underlining their credentials as a serious Premier League outfit.

That result adds further weight to the argument that the switch to 3-5-2 has transformed Leeds, with their remarkable resilience making them an increasingly difficult side to beat.

To illustrate just how good Leeds have been since the end of November 2025, here is the Premier League table since they switched to a 3-5-2 formation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I was born in North Wales in 1980, and my first memory of football was playing for the school team as a kid.

As a nine or 10-year-old I started getting my cousin’s hand-me-down Everton shirts, and this certainly helped me decide which of the local sides I was going to follow!

The two red sides close by (Wrexham and the other lot) never once turned my head.

According to recent reports, and then, in 1991, my mind was made up for good. My uncle asked me if I’d like to go to watch Everton play.

It was the first ever game I’d been to watch live. It was at Bramall Lane, and I’ll never ever forget it.

My uncle got us to the ground early and took me and my cousin to wait for the players’ coach to turn up.

The coach arrived and as I was only a little kid at that point, my uncle lifted me up to get a glimpse of the players.

The first player I saw was substantial Neville Southall and I reached over to pat him on the back and wish him good luck. He glanced over his shoulder and gave me a wry smile.

Not only was I now hooked on Everton, but all I wanted to be from that point on was a goalkeeper.

A few years later I got to taste my first ever trophy win as an Evertonian. Me and my dad watched the whole FA Cup final build-up from Grandstand in the morning to Match of the Day, with the game in between.

We couldn’t get tickets to the final, but my uncle and cousin did go the Charity Shield.

Even though that was my last taste of silverware as an Evertonian, my love for this club has never wavered.

I’m now 46 years old, lived in Australia for 20 years and I’m happily married with seven children – six of which have all been to Goodison and the youngest has beat me to visit the new stadium last year!

My highlights of the last 35 years are:.

-              - My first game in 1991.

-              - 1995 and the FA Cup victory.

-              - Going to Howard’s testimonial a few months before leaving for Australia.

-              - Spending a day painting parts of Goodison in 2013.

-              - Goodison trips with my dad, cousins, uncle and taking my six kids to see the eventual champions in 2016.

-              -Taking my two sons to the games in Sydney.

-              - My daughter (who now lives in Rochdale) going to the last game at Goodison.

-              - And my wife taking our two youngest daughters to see our stone at the new ground last year.

I’ve got so many fond memories of our beautiful club, and I can’t wait to make millions more in the coming decades.

In a recent development, there is no other football club for me or my family. Once a Blue, always a Blue.

My Everton shares first-hand accounts describing the most-treasured memories of fans, players, and staff both past and present.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leeds United delivered a statement performance at Stamford Bridge, thumping Chelsea 4-1 to claim their first away victory against the Blues in more than a quarter of a century.

Noah Okafor scored twice to turn the game around after Emmanuel Emegha’s opener, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin converting from the spot and Brenden Aaronson adding a late fourth.

Sources indicate that “The last time this club was able to win here was last century. We have created history, but it doesn’t feel like this. We fully deserved to win this game, and it’s great for everyone connected with Leeds,” Leeds manager Daniel Farke told BBC Sport after the final whistle.

According to recent reports, “We came here to win the game. We spoke the whole week about this and wanted to make this our game where we play on the front foot. We didn’t want to allow Chelsea to control the mood.

Recent findings suggest that “We need to have good fitness levels and I have smart players who understand how we want to press and play. We have to be more concentrated to execute what we want to do. Desire is second to none, and we are competitive in the best league in the world.”.

In a recent development, the result has seen Leeds leapfrog Chelsea and move up to sixth in the Premier League table. They at the moment sit just one point off a potential Champions League qualification spot.

“People talk about turning points and we have to learn about stuff that didn’t work and try to better that,” said club captain Ethan Ampadu.

“We know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect – we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It’s right we can enjoy this performance.”.

“We have to be realistic and understand how hard this league is. We need to back this up next week, if we don’t then this performance is wasted. We know where we want to get Leeds back to. It could be a long road but we’re ready for it.”.

Here are 11 remarkable stats from Leeds’ big win away to Chelsea:.

– This was Leeds United’s first win at Stamford Bridge in the 21st century. Their last victory away at Chelsea came way back in December 1999.

– The rare away win for Leeds comes fresh from Chelsea’s defeat at home to Tottenham last month. That was Spurs’ only 2nd win at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League era. Two results that’ll take Xabi Alonso a long time to get over.

Industry observers note that – Since returning to the Premier League last year, Leeds are now unbeaten in eight league games against Chelsea, Manchester United and Liverpool. Three wins, five defeats.

– Since Farke switched to a back three last November, Leeds sit eighth in the Premier League table – they’ve sustained near European qualification-level results over almost a full season’s worth of results, and have taken more points than the likes of Chelsea, Tottenham and Newcastle.

– The scoreline was no fluke, Leeds comfortably beating the hosts on ‘expected goals’. Farke’s men notched 2.51xG compared to Chelsea’s 0.56xG.

– Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez was forced into twice as many saves (four) as his opposite number James Trafford (two).

Industry observers note that – Per the statistics, Chelsea created zero ‘big chances’. Leeds registered seven in total, missing four alongside the three that were converted. It could’ve been a bloodbath.

– Ethan Ampadu completed 88% of his passes (58/66), including 88% in the opposition half (30/34). Covered 12.4km, registered 11 ball recoveries, won three of four ground duels and wasn’t dribbled past once.

Sources indicate that – Noah Okafor scored twice from just three shots, come from an xG of just 0.3. He also created one substantial chance, played three key passes and notched three successful dribbles.

– Leeds covered 125.1km collectively, six kilometres more than Chelsea.

Recent findings suggest that – Only Brighton and Arsenal have conceded fewer goals than Leeds in the Premier League this season, and only Tottenham (12.4xG) and Arsenal (7.6xG) have better underlying numbers when it comes to ‘expected goals against’ this season. Leeds have faced 13.1xG from 11 outings in 2026-27.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cristiano Ronaldo took to social media on Thursday to announce that he had played his last game for Portugal.
  • "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No.
  • "I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cristiano Ronaldo took to social media on Thursday to announce that he had played his last game for Portugal.

"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team," the 41-year-old Ronaldo said in a video on his Instagram account.

"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo noted.

The former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus forward represented his country 234 times, scoring 146 goals — making him the men's record-holder for ⁠international ​appearances and for international goals.

He captained Portugal ​to their first major trophy at ​Euro 2016 and led them to the 2019 and 2025 Nations League titles.

"It was not an easy decision, there are decisions that are not ​only with the head. They are also made with the heart," Ronaldo continued in the Instagram post.

"If I ever made you happy, ​if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel ⁠proud ​of our country, then it ​was all worth it.".

He also thanked his family, the Portuguese people ​and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his national ​team career.

The Portuguese Football Association (FPF) released a statement expressing its gratitude and respect for the player also known as "CR7.".

"Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal's profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!" it read.

The FPF intends to organize a tribute "in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much.".

While his long-rival Lionel Messi ended his Argentina career with a much anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo's final appearance may go down as Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales on September 24, depending on the nature of the tribute. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus left him on the bench for the following match and said he wouldn't start the next one.

Ronaldo responded by walking out of the Portugal training camp. He was subsequently suspended and fined by the FPF, but he had been expected to return to Portugal for the November international break.

Like Messi, Ronaldo intends to continue his club career with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

In a recent development, and that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

In that instance, United fans booed Solskjaer. Carrick at least received some polite applause from the fans, who are a smart bunch and know the club’s problems extend far beyond the man in the dugout. Still, it is always the manager who pays the price. Solskjaer said he knew at half-time he was toast and Carrick is now under real threat himself – and seemingly at loggerheads with his captain.

Fernandes’s criticism of United’s set-up and approach was cutting and a direct attack on his manager and backroom team. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” the United captain remarked.

Recent findings suggest that carrick has been telling us for weeks that he and his squad are together, that the team are not too far away, that it is all about small margins. He even described Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Leeds as a “fresh start”. But Como blew the lid off any pretence of that being the case. Even by the standards of this season to date, though, what unfolded here in the rain in Lombardy was shocking to witness.

Como, inspired by the outstanding Nico Paz, were every bit as good as United – who have won just two of 11 games this season – were a pitiful mess.

Having conceded after just 47 seconds to Atlético Madrid last week, United were behind after only 118 seconds this time. That in itself told you a lot about these players and this team and it set the tone for what was to follow: a masterclass in incompetence and indifference. Michael Carrick has insisted there is not a “toxic culture” at Manchester United in the wake of scathing criticism from former manager Erik ten Hag of the Old Trafford hierarchy and player power at the club.

The current United manager – who is under pressure after the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years – also believes he has the backing of the United board, despite Ten Hag accusing Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos regime of a series of “broken promises”.

In an interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag blamed Ratcliffe and his executives for fuelling a “toxic culture” by giving power to players and failing to back him on disciplinary matters relating to Marcus Rashford, Jadon Sancho and other first-teamers.

But Carrick said he had not encountered any toxicity since taking over from Ruben Amorim in January and suggested United’s last two outings, a 1-1 draw against Leeds United and a 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid, underlined the camaraderie in the group.

“Since I came back, the players and the staff have given us everything that they could give,” Carrick remarked before Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Cesc Fàbregas’s Como in northern Italy, where he is battling an injury and illness crisis.

In a recent development, “We’ve had some good performances. We’ve had some performances that we want to do better and we can improve on. We’ve made some mistakes.

“But I have to say, the type of performance put into the weekend and for large parts against Atlético, there’s a lot of togetherness there. There’s a lot of will and determination to do better and wanting to do it for each other, which is crucial.”.

In a recent development, two wins – against Ipswich Town and Sabah – in United’s first 10 matches of the season, a public outburst from Lisandro Martínez and accusations of a “toxic culture” at the club have piled pressure on Carrick. And an uninspiring draw at Elland Road on Sunday did little to settle the rising tide of discontent within the United fanbase.

When asked for his team news, the first words that came from the United head coach’s mouth were: “Right, bit of mixed bag to be honest.” That was not a great sign, and Carrick will be without Martínez, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Ayden Heaven, Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu, who are injured, while Leny Yoro serves a suspension following his red card against Atlético Madrid.

Like United, the hosts are without a handful of key players, with Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao and Jesus Rodriguez missing from the match-day squad. The abundantly talented Argentine No 10 Nico Paz will feature, however, and he will be keen to showcase his talents in the Champions League.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Amazon rainforest plays a key part in the cycling of carbon and water on regional and global scales, and is widely viewed as a perennially evergreen ecosystem. However, writing in Nature, Song et al.1 report that there are extended periods when trees in most of the rainforest remain leafless. Known as deciduousness, this state occurs between the shedding of old leaves and the emergence and early development (flushing) of fresh ones. The authors also found that hydroclimatic conditions such as annual rainfall have a more crucial role in determining this pattern of leaf behaviour than do soil properties and light availability. The seasonal variation in tropical leaf cover and photosynthetic activity in the Amazon observed by the authors is less pronounced than that seen for broadleaf trees in temperate and boreal climate zones.

#83150. Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?
